title: WA Residential Design Codes (R-Codes) Volume 1
disclaimer: PLANNING, NOT BUILDING CODE. The R-Codes set what may be built on a lot -- setbacks, site cover, open space -- and are a separate instrument from the NCC, which sets how it must be built. Both apply. Controls are keyed by the R-code density of the lot, so the answer is wrong unless the right one is given: pass --zone R20 or whatever the certificate of title or local scheme says. Local Development Plans and structure plans routinely override these figures for a specific estate, and where one exists it governs. Boundary walls, overshadowing, garage width and street surveillance are not encoded. Visual privacy is, in the separate au-wa-privacy pack, but simplified to a perpendicular setback rather than the cone of vision the R-Codes actually swing -- read that pack's disclaimer before relying on it.

site.$comment: Keyed by R-code. Confirm against the lot's Local Development Plan, which commonly varies these.

rules.title: Site cover
rules.message: Site cover is {coverage_ratio} of the lot; this density allows {max_coverage_ratio}.
rules.note: Checked against the cover this lot's density code actually allows, not against a fixed figure. It used to assert 0.50 -- R20's number -- so a plan built to R60's 0.70 was reported as breaching a control it met. Where no density has been supplied the control is missing and this reports unchecked, which is the honest answer: the limit depends on a code nobody has given.

rules.title: Primary street setback
rules.message: The primary street setback is {setback_front_mm} mm; this density requires {min_setback_front_mm} mm.
rules.note: Checked against this lot's density code. It used to assert 4000 mm regardless, so every R60 and R80 plan -- which the R-Codes set at 2000 -- was reported as breaching the setback it was built to. The R-Codes permit averaging against adjoining lots, which is still not modelled.

rules.title: Outdoor living area
rules.clause: R-Codes Vol 1, Part C (outdoor living area)
rules.message: The outdoor living area is {outdoor_living_m2} m2 at the {outdoor_living_where} of the lot, {outdoor_living_min_dim_mm} mm across at its narrowest; this density requires {min_outdoor_living_m2} m2 and {min_outdoor_living_dim_mm} mm.
rules.note: TWO LIMBS, TESTED TOGETHER. The R-Codes set an area AND a minimum dimension, and an area met by a long thin strip does not comply -- on a narrow lot the widest open rectangle is often the 1 m ribbon down a side boundary, which satisfies the area on paper and is not somewhere anybody sits. Only the area figure is encoded here, so until the dimension is supplied this reports UNCHECKED rather than passing on one limb of a two-limb control. Measured as ONE rectangle of open ground outside the street setback; a roofed alfresco is not counted, though the R-Codes let part of one count, because how much is not a figure this pack carries. That it must be accessible from a habitable room is not modelled.

rules.title: Building height
rules.message: The building is {overall_height_mm} mm from floor level to the ridge; the limit here is {max_height_mm} mm.
rules.note: MEASURED TO THE RIDGE, and the figure supplied has to be the same measurement. Instruments differ: some set a limit to the top of the external wall, some to the top of the roof, and some set both. The wall height is carried as well, so a second rule can be written against it once it is known which this figure is. Height is also measured from natural ground level, which this model does not carry -- it measures from the floor, so a house on fill or a sloping lot will read low here. Nothing here has supplied the limit: until one is, this reports unchecked.

design.$comment: Regional construction practice, not a code requirement. Override per project.
